problem.paragraph: Find the horizontal and vertical asymptotes of the graph of the function

solution.paragraph: we see that $$y = 2$$ is a horizontal asymptote. Next, since

implies $$x = - 1$$ or $$x = 1$$ , these are candidates for the vertical asymptotes of the graph of $$f$$ . Since the numerator of $$f$$ is not equal to zero for $$x = - 1$$ or $$x = 1$$ , we conclude that $$x = - 1$$ and $$x = 1$$ are vertical asymptotes of the graph of $$f$$ .

problem.paragraph: Sketch the graph of the function

solution.paragraph: We obtain the following information on the graph of $$f$$ .

list.item: (1) The domain of $$f$$ is the interval $$\left( {- \infty,\infty} \right)$$ .
(2) By setting $$x = 0$$ , we find that the $$y$$ -intercept is $$4$$ .

(3) Since $$\begin{array}{rcl} {\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow - \infty}f(x)} & = & {\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow - \infty}\left( {\frac{2}{3}x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 6x + 4} \right) = - \infty} \\ {\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}f(x)} & = & {\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}\left( {\frac{2}{3}x^{3} - 2x^{2} - 6x + 4} \right) = \infty} \end{array}$$ we see that $$f(x)$$ decreases without bound as $$x$$ decreases without bound and that $$f(x)$$ increases without bound as $$x$$ increases without bound.
(4) Since $$f$$ is a polynomial function, the graph of $$f$$ has no asymptotes.

(5) $$\begin{array}{l} {{f^{\prime}{(x)}} = {2x^{2} - 4x - 6 = 2{({x^{2} - 2x - 3})}}} \\ {\phantom{f^{\prime}{(x)}} = {2{({x + 1})}{({x - 3})}}} \end{array}$$ Setting $$f^{\prime}(x) = 0$$ gives $$x = - 1$$ or $$x = 3$$ . The accompanying sign diagram for $$f^{\prime}$$ shows that $$f$$ is increasing on the intervals $$\left( {- \infty, - 1} \right)$$ and $$\left( {3,\infty} \right)$$ and decreasing on $$\left( {- 1,3} \right)$$ . Details A sign diagram with a number line labeled x with tick marks between negative 3 to 4 with the marks negative 1, 0 and 3 labeled. Above the number line plus symbols appear from the left extreme till just before the mark negative 1 and just after the mark 3 till the right extreme. The number 0 appears just above the marks negative 1 and 3. Minus symbols appear from just after 0 to just before 3.

(6) From the results of Step 5, we see that $$x = - 1$$ and $$x = 3$$ are critical numbers of $$f$$ . Furthermore, the sign diagram of $$f^{\prime}$$ tells us that $$x = - 1$$ gives rise to a relative maximum of $$f$$ and $$x = 3$$ gives rise to a relative minimum of $$f$$ . Now, $$\begin{array}{rcl} {f{({- 1})}} & = & {\frac{2}{3}{({- 1})}^{3} - 2{({- 1})}^{2} - 6{({- 1})} + 4 = \frac{22}{3}} \\ {f{(3)}} & = & {\frac{2}{3}{(3)}^{3} - 2{(3)}^{2} - 6{(3)} + 4 = - 14} \end{array}$$ so $$f\left( {- 1} \right) = \frac{22}{3}$$ is a relative maximum of $$f$$ and $$f(3) = - 14$$ is a relative minimum of $$f$$ .

(7) $$f^{''}(x) = 4x - 4 = 4(x - 1)$$ which is equal to zero when $$x = 1$$ . The accompanying sign diagram of $$f^{''}$$ shows that the graph of $$f$$ is concave downward on the interval $$\left( {- \infty,1} \right)$$ and concave upward on the interval $$\left( {1,\infty} \right)$$ . Details A sign diagram with a number line labeled x with two tick marks labeled 0 and 1. Above the number line minus symbols appear from the left extreme till just before the mark 1. The number 0 appears just above the mark 1 followed by plus symbols then appear just after the mark 1 and extends to the right extreme.

(8) From the results of Step 7, we see that $$x = 1$$ is the only candidate for an inflection point of $$f$$ . Since $$f^{''}(x)$$ changes sign as we move across the point $$x = 1$$ and $$f(1) = \frac{2}{3}(1)^{3} - 2(1)^{2} - 6(1) + 4 = - \frac{10}{3}$$ we see that the required inflection point is $$\left( {1, - \frac{10}{3}} \right)$$ .

(9) Summarizing this information, we have the following: Domain: $$\left( {- \infty,\infty} \right)$$ Intercept: $$\left( {0,4} \right)$$ $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow - \infty}f(x)$$ ; $$\lim\limits_{x\rightarrow\infty}f(x)$$ : $$- \infty$$ ; $$\infty$$ Asymptotes: None Intervals where $$f$$ is $$\nearrow$$ or $$\searrow$$ : $$\nearrow$$ on $$\left( {- \infty, - 1} \right)$$ and $$\left( {3,\infty} \right)$$ ; $$\searrow$$ on $$\left( {- 1,3} \right)$$ Relative extrema: Rel. max. at $$\left( {- 1,\frac{22}{3}} \right)$$ ; rel. min. at $$\left( {3, - 14} \right)$$ Concavity: Downward on $$\left( {- \infty,1} \right)$$ ; upward on $$\left( {1,\infty} \right)$$ Point of inflection: $$\left( {1, - \frac{10}{3}} \right)$$ The graph of $$f$$ is sketched in the accompanying figure. Details A curve y = (2/3) x^3 minus 2 x^2 minus 6 x + 4 is graphed on the x y coordinate plane. The x axis is marked from negative 3 to 5 and the y axis is marked from negative 14 to 9. The curve enters the third quadrant at around (negative 3, negative 14), rises steeply upward to the right, concave down, cuts the x axis at around (negative 2.3, 0), rises upward to the right concave down till a high point at (negative 1, 7), descends to the right, still concave down, cuts the y axis at (0, 4), briefly crosses the first quadrant, cuts the x axis again at around (0.8, 0), descends to the right into the fourth quadrant, concave down till around (1.5, negative 5) where it inflects and then descends downward to the right, now concave up. The curve then reaches a low point at around (3, 14), rises upward to the right, cuts the x axis again at around (4.8, 0), and then rises into the first quadrant, concave up, till about (5, 7).

problem.paragraph: Terminal Velocity A skydiver leaps from the gondola of a hot-air balloon. As she free-falls, air resistance, which is proportional to her velocity, builds up to a point at which it balances the force due to gravity. The resulting motion may be described in terms of her velocity as follows: Starting at rest (zero velocity), her velocity increases and approaches a constant velocity, called the terminal velocity. Sketch a graph of her velocity $$\upsilon$$ versus time $$t$$ .

image.alt: Details A curve is graphed on a coordinate plane. The horizontal axis is labeled t and the vertical axis is labeled v. From an unlabeled point on the vertical axis, a dashed line runs to the right, parallel to the horizontal axis and is labeled Terminal velocity. The curve is entirely below the dashed line and begins at the origin, rises upward, almost linearly, to the right, concave down, and veers towards the dashed line, running parallel to it as it proceeds to the right.

problem.paragraph: Spread of a Flu Epidemic Initially, $$10$$ students at a junior high school contracted influenza. The flu spread over time, and the total number of students who eventually contracted the flu approached but never exceeded $$200$$ . Let $$P(t)$$ denote the number of students who had contracted the flu after $$t$$ days, where $$P$$ is an appropriate function.

list.item: Make a sketch of the graph of $$P$$ . (Your answer will not be unique.)
Where is the function increasing?
Does the graph of $$P$$ have a horizontal asymptote? If so, what is it?
Discuss the concavity of the graph of $$P$$ . Explain its significance.
Is there an inflection point on the graph of $$P$$ ? If so, explain its significance.
